rv.q: Its current production of “Native Son,” Nambi E. Kelley’s adaptation of Richard Wright’s 1940 novel, is one of the best Lifeline shows I’ve seen.
The stellar performances and Duncan’s incisive direction make this adaptation a must-see, offering a powerful reminder of the enduring relevance of Wright’s work.
Lifeline’s production is drama at its best.
Beyond this problem, this is a good and necessary show.

cn.t: Lifeline's "Native Son" delivers a brutal, powerful adaptation that stays true to Wright's novel while highlighting Bigger Thomas's unexpected vulnerability through masterful performances and incisive staging.
